instruction:
Sculpt an Adaptively-Tessellated Bent Tentacle with Sculptris Pro + SnakeHook

The file at C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\scene.obj contains a ZBrush Tool whose first (and only) SubTool, named TentStart, is a short cylinder of height 0.4 BU, radius 0.15 BU, aligned along the Y axis and centred at origin. The cylinder has 16 side segments with capped top and bottom; total ~64 triangular\quad faces. No polygroups beyond default, no UVs, no polypaint.

Load this OBJ into ZBrush, enable Sculptris Pro (adaptive dynamic tessellation), use the SnakeHook brush to pull the top end of the cylinder into a bent tentacle with three ~90 deg bends and a tapered tip, and export the result as C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.obj (OBJ format).

The exported C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.obj must satisfy:

- Exactly one SubTool, still named TentStart.
- Face count at least 300 (Sculptris Pro densifies the 64-face cylinder into hundreds of faces along the pulled path).
- When the mesh is sliced into cross-section rings along its principal axis, the ring-centroid polyline exhibits at least 2 bend points (local tangent change > 60 deg).
- The tip ring's mean radius is at most 25% of the root ring's mean radius (confirming tapering).
- Ring density (vertices per ring) in the bend regions is at least 1.2x the density in straight regions (confirming adaptive tessellation).
